title: Chicken and Dumplings
shortDescription: Thick chicken stew with fluffy dropped dumplings — not brothy soup
subtitle: Thick chicken stew with fluffy dropped dumplings — not brothy soup
description: Thick chicken stew with fluffy dropped dumplings — not brothy soup

steps.title: Brown chicken and build the stew base
steps.instruction: Pat chicken dry. Brown thighs in butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high, skin-side down first, 8–10 minutes total; transfer out. In the same pot, cook onion, carrot, celery, and garlic with salt until softened, 8 minutes. Stir in ¼ cup flour and cook 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer until stew-thick
steps.instruction: Add broth, bay leaves, and thyme. Return chicken. Simmer partially covered 30–35 minutes until chicken is tender. Stew should coat a spoon — not thin brothy soup. Shred or chop chicken, return meat, and discard skin and bones if you used bone-in.

steps.title: Mix dumpling batter
steps.instruction: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Cut in cold butter, then stir in milk and eggs until a thick, scoopable batter forms — thicker than pancake batter, it should mound on a spoon.

steps.title: Drop dumplings and steam
steps.instruction: Bring stew to a gentle simmer. Drop batter by ¼-cup scoops on top, spacing across the pot. Cover tightly and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid — dumplings steam and puff. Consistency when done: thick stew underneath, fluffy dumplings on top, not submerged thin soup.

steps.title: Finish and hold for late crew
steps.instruction: Dumplings are done when a skewer through a centre comes out clean. Stir parsley at the edge of the pot. Hold covered off heat up to 20 minutes or keep on lowest simmer — do not boil hard or dumplings fall apart. Ladle stew and dumplings together so each bowl gets both.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Chicken and Dumplings on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thick chicken stew with fluffy dropped dumplings — not brothy soup. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
